header.running_head: 3. The Rights and Duties of Muslims

blocks.arabic_text: اِنِّيْ خَادِمُهَا، فَقَالَ رَسُوْلُ اللهِ ﷺ: اِسْتَاْذِنْ عَلَيْهَا اَتُحِبُّ اَنْ تَرَاهَا عُرْيَانَةً؟ قَالَ: لَا، قَالَ: فَاسْتَاْذِنْ عَلَيْهَا.
blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه الامام مالك في الموطا، باب في الاستعذان، ص:٧٢٥
blocks.tamil_translation: Hazrat Ata ibn Yasar (RH) narrates: A man asked the Prophet ﷺ, “Ya Rasulallah! Must I ask my mother's permission to enter my mother's room?” He replied, “Yes.” He said, “My mother and I live in the same house!” The Prophet ﷺ said, “Go in only after taking permission.” He asked again, “I am the one who serves her” (so I have to go in and out often). Rasulullah ﷺ asked, “Go in only after taking permission! Would you like to see your mother in a state without clothes?” He said, “I would not like that.” The Prophet ﷺ said, “In that case, go in after taking permission!”

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ هُزَيْلٍ رَحِمَهُ اللهُ قَالَ: جَاءَ سَعْدٌ ﵁ فَوَقَفَ عَلَي بَابِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ يَسْتَاْذِنُ فَقَامَ مُسْتَقْبِلَ الْبَابِ فَقَالَ لَهُ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: هكَذَا عَنْكَ اَوْ هكَذَا فَاِنَّمَا اْلاِسْتِئْذَانُ مِنَ النَّظَرِ.
blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه ابوداؤد باب في الاستئذان رقم:٥١٧٤
blocks.tamil_translation: Hazrat Huzail (RH) narrates: Hazrat Sa'd (RA) came and, to ask permission (to go in) at the door of the Prophet's ﷺ (house), stood facing the door directly. Rasulullah ﷺ said to Hazrat Sa'd (RA): “(Do not stand facing the door directly; rather) stand to the right or to the left! (The reason: by standing facing the door, there is a chance of one's gaze going inside.) Asking permission has been prescribed precisely so that the gaze does not go inside.'

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ اَبِيْ هُرَيْرَةَ ﵁ اَنَّ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ قَالَ: اِذَا دَخَلَ الْبَصَرُ فَلَا
